summary: Phase S3 passes UX applicability review as explicitly not applicable. The track-owned changes from remediation baseline 2bddadc7 through the completed independent reviews at 4565377b are confined to Measure evidence, PostgreSQL/Drizzle schema and migration work, provider-neutral Domain persistence contracts and adapters, package metadata, and automated tests. No app route, page, component, browser-executed handler, JSX/TSX, style, or other user-visible surface changed, so starting a browser would not exercise this feature.
nonblocking_findings: The raw repository range 2bddadc7..4565377b contains interleaved APK-track commits with user-visible app paths. Those commits are independently owned by the APK track and are not Phase S3 mastery persistence changes; they must receive browser verification in their own acceptance workflow rather than being attributed to this package-only phase.
evidence: The 13 Phase S3 mastery/remediation commits after baseline 2bddadc7, including the strategy-only dependency-direction correction, change 38 unique track-owned paths: 7 Measure artifacts, 11 packages/db paths, and 20 packages/domain paths.

The track-owned path inventory has zero files under apps/, zero app or pages directories, zero page.tsx, layout.tsx, or route.ts/route.tsx files, zero component directories, and zero .tsx, .jsx, .css, or .scss files.

The production changes are seven school-scoped database tables and migrations plus provider-neutral Zod contracts, a transport-independent service, and in-memory/Drizzle persistence adapters. They expose no HTTP route, React component, navigation entry, browser storage, or presentation state.
A focused React/Next import scan across packages/domain/src/mastery, packages/db/src/schema/mastery.ts, and the Phase S3 persistence tests found no React or Next.js import or require usage.

The three independent Phase S3 audits already report no route-parity violation; the correctness and API audits independently identify browser runtime verification as not applicable because the phase exposes no route, component, or user-visible UI.

No browser session was started. With no browser-reachable production surface in the Phase S3 diff, an empty browser run would provide no feature evidence and could accidentally test unrelated concurrent Codecamp or APK work instead.

ux_applicability_justification: Phase S3 changes persistence contracts, service/adapters, database schema/migrations, tests, package metadata, and Measure artifacts only. It changes no browser-reachable route, page, component, handler, or presentation asset. Browser verification remains mandatory for the later user-facing Codecamp tracks, but has no valid target in this package-only phase.
